newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Albanians indicted on "terror" charges in Serbia.
newsitem.headline: Albanians indicted on "terror" charges in Serbia.

text.p: Serbian authorities in the troubled province of Kosovo on Thursday indicted 15 ethnic Albanians on charges of terrorism.

The latest indictment charges Albanians with killing three policemen and one Serb civilian and with attempting to murder 16 more persons, deputy district prosecutor in the provincial capital of Pristina Jovica Jovanovic told Reuters.
The Albanians belonged to one of the largest Albanian terrorist groups which operated in Kosovo in the period from 1992 - 1996, he said.
During the arrest of the group large quantities of hand grenades, rifles with telescopic sights and automatic rifles were found in their possession, the indictment says.
Only their leaders Besim Rama from Gornji Prekaz and Avni Nura from Prelovac are in custody while other members will be tried in absentia. The date for their trial has not been set.
Last Friday, the Serbian authorities charged 18 ethnic Albanians with trying to force the secession of the province.
Albanian parties deny the existence of terrorist groups and say those arrested are victims of Serb persecution.
Some 30 people, both Serbs and Albanians, have been killed over the past year as guerrilla violence struck the volatile province where ethnic Albanians outnumber Serbs nine to one.
Serbian police cracked down on the province in January arresting some 70 people in a widely-pubicised sweep following the guerrilla attacks.
Serbia revoked Kosovo's autonomy in 1989 claiming its Albanian population wanted to secede and join neighbouring Albania.
The province is widely regarded as a powderkeg that could destroy international peace efforts in the Balkans.
The latest indictment comes less than two weeks ahead of scheduled talks in New York on April 7 between Serb and ethnic Albanian leaders on Kosovo's status.
